_readme: FIAT STAGE PLATES (6 Nov, Matt: "include the new backdrops and items from yesterday"; docs/design/stages.md §6): a plate for each site's 2/3 and 3/3, 24 jobs at 744x320, $0.15 each (about $3.60).

Out art/fight_new/<site>_2_plate.png / _3_plate.png: RunView.stage_key finds them by name and stands each on its site's own wall (art/fight_walls/), the site's placed slots till F3 places the stage's - nothing to wire.
Each styled on its site's plate (palette, light, painting style), the same viewpoint and layout family, a different spot of the same place. ++ --parallel 3.
Regenerate with python3 tools/make_stage_plates_manifest.py; check with python3 tools/art_lint.py.

jobs.description: A first-person view at crouching eye level, as if from behind cover in a light-gun arcade game, looking further into the overgrown allotments: plastic water butts tipped over on their sides, a puddle spread from them, sheds with their doors torn off and lying in the weeds, rows of broken bean canes, a dark open shed doorway on the left. Nobody in the scene, empty and waiting. No people or figures anywhere. Composed for three figures to stand in later: clear open ground in the middle distance just right of centre, a dark doorway or gap on the left side well down the scene, and room in the right foreground. The ground runs across the lower third; the horizon sits a third of the way down. One continuous scene edge to edge: no repeated sections, no seams. The bottom fifth of the scene is plain open ground running to the frame's edge, nothing standing in the foreground: no walls, rubble or cover there, it is drawn over later. Only the palette, light and painting style of the style image, not its view or its subject: this is a different spot of the same place, seen from the same crouching viewpoint, with the same layout of near, middle and far ground. The painting fills the whole canvas to all four edges, no border, frame or margin. Every board, panel, screen and label in it blank, no lettering, numbers or pictures anywhere. Realistic painted pixel art, soft overcast light, muted cool northern palette, worn and lived-in, post-collapse Britain on a grey day; no black outlines, not anime, not a cartoon, not glossy; no text, no logos.
